one_month_reasoning: 2026-10-31 is a Saturday, so the relevant print is the Oct 30 close. (1) Q3 2026 results: Earnings Whispers and AAII both list Oct 28, but Hudbay has not confirmed it. Hudbay's 2026 6-Ks came about two weeks earlier than in 2025 (Q1 May 1 vs May 13, Q2 Jul 29 vs Aug 13), and it normally announces the call about three weeks ahead, so I put about 65% on the print landing inside the window. Consensus is $0.36-0.37 (9 analysts) against Q2's $0.28 actual. That is a high bar: Q3 benefits from H2 grade sequencing, the Copper Mountain SAG repair and about 10kt of delayed Peru concentrate shipped in early July, but gold now ($4,187) is below the Q2 average ($4,508). I expect roughly an in-line print with little drift. (2) Copper World DFS/sanction: the primary filings say 'late 2026' / 'later in 2026', so I no longer treat it as likely inside October. I put maybe 25% on it landing in the window. A capex number above the 2023 PFS is already flagged, which makes the sign of that event ambiguous. (3) The Sep 28 Snow Lake mine-plan upgrade and the Oct 1 site visit are fresh positives, and Oct 2 opened about +4% ($27.20 on light volume); I give that open only a small weight. Net: median about $26.4 (slightly above $26.18) and monthly sigma about 18% (63%/3.5, widened a little for the probable earnings event), close to symmetric. Over a month, copper and gold moves dominate, and I take no view on them.

fair_value.method: Blend of 2027E EV/EBITDA (6.5x on ~$1.75B, less ~$20M attributable net debt -> $25.6, 35%), 2027E P/E (15x on ~$1.81 EPS with no Copper Mountain NCI -> $27.2, 30%) and P/NAV (1.1x on a $24.6/sh NAV at $5.00/lb Cu and $3,300/oz Au with Copper Mountain at 100%, Copper World 70% at $1.5B and Cactus at $1.1B -> $27.0, 35%) = $26.6.

The 2027 guidance range of 213-269koz has a midpoint of about 241koz. The Sep 28 Snow Lake plan has Snow Lake at 186koz in 2027 (201koz in 2026), which fits the midpoint once Copper Mountain and Constancia gold are added.
Spot is about $6.5/lb (LME). Hudbay's own Sep 2026 deck uses $5.80 for 2027 and $5.00 long-term. I take about 12% off spot for mean reversion, which is close to the company's 2027 deck.

Spot is about $4,187 and the company's 2027 deck is $4,200. I haircut spot about 7% to $3,900, then take off about 4% for the Wheaton stream, in line with Q2's $4,312 realized against the $4,508 market average. Raised from $3,700 in round 1.
Snow Lake zinc 28kt in 2027 per the Sep plan, silver (company deck $70/oz) and Constancia moly.
H1 2026 revenue of $1,388.6M less adjusted EBITDA of $743.1M is $645M per half, about $1.3B a year. I add a little for inflation and higher throughput.
Mid-tier copper producers trade around 5.5-8x forward EBITDA. 6.5x reflects a near-net-cash balance sheet (net debt/EBITDA -0.1x) and the US growth pipeline, offset by Copper World capex from 2027.

Reported net cash is $80.5M (cash $890.9M, debt $860.2M), but $334.5M of that cash is held by Copper World LLC, is restricted to the project and is 30% Mitsubishi's. So -80.5 + 0.3 x 334.5 = about +$20M net debt attributable to Hudbay.
444,144,760 at June 30, 2026 (FS note 21b), after 46.8M shares were issued for Arizona Sonoran. The NCIB was unused as of Q2.

bear.story: Copper falls toward $4.5/lb and gold toward $3,200 as the cycle cools. Copper World DFS capex comes in well above $2B and sanction slips or needs heavy funding. Copper Mountain keeps missing throughput, so 2027 lands near the 140kt low end. Peru political or social disruption hits Constancia. EBITDA about $1.1B at about 5.5x.

base.story: About 150-160kt Cu and 240koz Au in 2027 at Cu $5.5-6/lb and Au about $3,800-4,000. Copper World sanctioned around year-end 2026 with Mitsubishi's $180M paid by about July 2027. The balance sheet stays near net cash, Snow Lake keeps delivering about 185koz, and the stock re-rates modestly on the volume step-up.

bull.story: The copper-deficit narrative holds, with Cu above $7/lb and Au above $4,000. 2027 production comes in at the top of 140-184kt, Copper World is built on budget with project finance, and Cactus/Mason studies show a path to about 500kt. NTM EBITDA about $2.6B at 7x.

thesis_break_reason: Below about $16 (about -39%, near the bear case and above the $14.34 52-week low), market cap would be about $7.1B. That is roughly 4x my 2027E EBITDA of $1.75B and about 4.5x even a $1.55B haircut case, with no credit for Copper World (Mitsubishi implies at least about $1.4B for Hudbay's 70%) or Cactus (about $1.1B paid in stock). Trading there would most likely mean a sustained copper break below about $4.5/lb, a Copper World capex or funding shock forcing equity issuance, or a major operating failure (Constancia/Peru, Copper Mountain short of its ramp), rather than ordinary 60%-vol noise.

reasoning: Hudbay Minerals is a copper-gold producer worth about $11.6B (444.1M shares after the Arizona Sonoran deal). It has about $20M of attributable net debt (reported net cash $80.5M, but $334.5M of that is restricted to Copper World LLC and 30% belongs to Mitsubishi), H1 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $743M, and guided 2027 copper of 140-184kt against 110-138kt for 2026. The supervisor's fact checks changed four inputs, and I verified each in the primary filings. First, Copper Mountain is 100% owned (Q2 MD&A). That raises my NAV by about $0.5B and removes a $0.04B NCI deduction from EPS. Second, Copper World sanction is 'late 2026', not 'early Q4'. Third, Cactus should be valued at about $1.1B (stock consideration), not $1.27B. Fourth, net debt should be attributable when Copper World is valued at 70%. I had also overstated Copper World by scaling the PFS too aggressively; the PFS's own +$0.6B per $0.50/lb sensitivity gives about $1.5B for 70%. The new Sep 28 Snow Lake 6-K adds a reserve life to 2043, 186koz of 2027 gold and the company's own price deck (Cu $5.80 for 2027 and $5.00 long-term; Au $4,200 for 2027 and $3,600 long-term). That deck supports my $5.75 copper and led me to raise gold to $3,900 market ($3,750 realized after the stream) and the NAV deck to $5.00/$3,300. The corrections roughly offset: Copper Mountain and the deck go up, while Copper World, Cactus and net debt go down. My three methods are $25.6, $27.2 and $27.0, which blend to $26.6, about 2% above spot. So on haircut prices the stock is roughly fairly valued. The upside is mostly a call on copper and gold staying near records plus pipeline option value; the downside is a metals reversal or a Copper World capex shock. I disagree mildly with the supervisor's lean toward $28: an EV/EBITDA lens on consolidated EBITDA, at a sensible mid-tier multiple and with consistent attributable net debt, still lands near $25-26. The scenarios (bear $15/25%, base $28/50%, bull $40/25%) give a mean of about $27.75. The ladder is a lognormal with median about $26.7 and sigma 0.48. That sigma is below the 63% realized vol, because the past year included a +77% re-rating and the balance sheet limits distress, but well above large-cap norms. I fattened the far-left tail for mining event risk. The net change from round 1 is small, a slight upward tilt above about $21. Research this round was limited to primary filings: the Snow Lake 6-K, the Q2 MD&A and the EDGAR filing index, which shows no Copper World sanction filing as of Oct 2.
